The electoral count in 1824
column2: Jackson won 99 electoral votes, Adams 84, Crawford 41, and Clay 37, so with no majority the House, under the Twelfth Amendment, chose among the top three.

column1: When the "corrupt bargain" charge was born
column2: In 1825 the House elected John Quincy Adams, and two days later Adams named Henry Clay secretary of state, launching the 1828 campaign.

column1: Voter turnout from 1824 to 1840
column2: Turnout rose from 27 percent in 1824 to 56 percent in 1828 and 78 percent in 1840, probably the highest in U.S. history.

column1: When Jackson was elected president
column2: Jackson, already a late surge in 1824, won handily in 1828 with enormous southern majorities and was reelected in 1832 against Henry Clay.

column1: When the Indian Removal Act passed, and Worcester v. Georgia
column2: Congress passed the Indian Removal Act in 1830, and in 1832 the Marshall Court decided Worcester v. Georgia, a ruling Jackson called "stillborn" and ignored.

column1: The Trail of Tears
column2: In 1838 Van Buren had the army round up the Cherokees, and about 15,000 were forced west on the Trail of Tears, of whom about one-quarter died, including John Ross's wife.

column1: How much Indian land Jackson's treaties took
column2: Jackson concluded nearly 70 treaties by which the United States acquired about 100 million acres, and he had personally obtained large shares of Tennessee, Florida, Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, Kentucky, and North Carolina.

column1: When the Denmark Vesey plot was alleged
column2: In 1822 Denmark Vesey and 34 others were hanged in Charleston and 37 were banished, after an alleged plot to seize the city.

column1: When the Nullification Crisis peaked
column2: A South Carolina convention in November 1832 declared the tariffs of 1828 and 1832 void after February 1, 1833; Jackson issued his proclamation in December 1832, and he signed the compromise tariff and the Force Bill on March 1, 1833.

column1: When the Tariff of Abominations and the Exposition and Protest appeared
column2: The Tariff of Abominations passed in 1828, and South Carolina answered that year with the Exposition and Protest.

column1: When the Webster-Hayne debate took place
column2: Robert Hayne and Daniel Webster debated nullification in the Senate in 1830.

column1: When Jackson vetoed the Bank and removed the deposits
column2: Biddle applied for recharter in 1832, four years early; Jackson vetoed it that year, removed the deposits in 1833 through Roger Taney, and the charter expired in 1836 with no national bank to replace it.

column1: How many bills Jackson vetoed
column2: Jackson vetoed 12 bills, compared with 9 by all previous presidents combined, and he vetoed on policy grounds, not only constitutionality.

column1: The land and banking boom before 1837
column2: State banknotes rose from $82 million in January 1835 to $120 million in December 1836, the number of banks from 329 in 1829 to 788 in 1837, and public land sales from $2.6 million in 1832 to about $25 million in 1836.

column1: When the Specie Circular was issued, and the panics that followed
column2: Jackson issued the Specie Circular in July 1836; the Panic of 1837 came less than two months after Van Buren's inauguration, and in 1839 the cotton market bottomed out into a severe depression, with wages falling 30 to 50 percent.

column1: When the Whig Party was organized, and the 1836 result
column2: The Whig Party was organized in 1834, and in 1836 Democrat Martin Van Buren beat three Whig sectional candidates.

column1: The 1840 election result
column2: About 900,000 new voters appeared from 1836 to 1840, nearly four-fifths of eligible voters turned out, and Harrison led by about 150,000 of 2.4 million popular votes, winning 234 electoral votes to Van Buren's 60.

column1: Free Black voting limits in the North
column2: By 1840 about 171,000 free Blacks lived in the North; Black men could vote equally only in five New England states, and New York's $250 property requirement, after 1821, disenfranchised about 90 percent of adult Black males.

column1: When the American Colonization Society and Liberia were founded
column2: The American Colonization Society was founded in 1816, and it established Liberia in 1821-1822; David Walker's Appeal appeared in 1829.

column1: When Black Hawk and the Seminoles resisted
column2: Black Hawk's Sauk and Fox force was crushed in 1832, and Osceola's Seminoles held out in Florida until 1842.
